note: V90Jd.cpp is the constructor, the destructor and the two packing leaves.  The constructor is where this set is aimed: it is fourteen stores and two loops, and the whole of what it can get wrong is WHICH bit of the parameter reaches WHICH byte of the message.  So most of the mutations below transpose a pair or move a loop bound by one -- the failures a comparison of the two objects can see and a reading of the disassembly can miss.  Two entries cover the CRC in getBitVector so the file's older half is not left unmeasured now that it has a suite. A destructor-store mutation in this file WAS recorded `equivalent` on the grounds that GCC deletes a store to `*this` in a destructor. That was measured and true; `-fno-lifetime-dse` in CXXFLAGS then restored GCC 3.4.2's semantics and the store survives, so the mutation is caught and the verdict is retired. If that flag is ever dropped, this entry goes back to being uncatchable -- and the symptom will be a NOT CAUGHT, not a compile error.
